title: Mushroom Risotto
subtitle: Creamy Arborio rice with porcini and chestnut mushrooms
excerpt: A deeply savoury risotto made with a blend of dried porcini and fresh chestnut mushrooms, stirred slowly in warm stock until the rice is creamy and each grain has a slight bite.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto is the foundational dish of the Po Valley in northern Italy, where short-grain rice varieties — Arborio, Carnaroli, and Vialone Nano — have been cultivated since the fifteenth century. The dish is defined by the gradual addition of warm stock to the rice while stirring, which encourages the starch to release slowly into the cooking liquid, creating the characteristic creamy consistency without the addition of cream. The technique differs from pilaf (in which the rice is left alone) and from boiled rice: the constant stirring and incremental liquid addition is what makes risotto risotto. Mushroom risotto (risotto ai funghi) is one of the most classic variations. Dried porcini, rehydrated in warm water, provide an intense base of flavour; fresh mushrooms add texture. The porcini soaking water is used as part of the stock to avoid wasting any flavour. The dish is finished with cold butter and Parmesan, beaten vigorously off the heat in a technique called mantecatura, which creates the final emulsified creaminess.

recipeTools.notes: A wide, deep saucepan or saute pan for the risotto.

content.text: Keep the stock hot throughout cooking: adding cold stock arrests the cooking and cools the starch, breaking the creamy texture. A ladle at a time is the right pace: each addition should be stirred in and mostly absorbed before the next goes in. The risotto is done when the rice is tender with a slight bite in the very centre and the whole mass flows slowly when the pan is tilted. Beat in cold butter and Parmesan off the heat, then cover and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

items.preparation: soaked in 300 ml boiling water for 20 minutes, liquid strained and reserved
kept warm in a separate saucepan
cold, cut in cubes; 30 g for cooking, 30 g for finishing

content.text: Add the strained porcini soaking liquid to the vegetable stock in the saucepan and keep warm over low heat. Chop the rehydrated porcini roughly. Fry the fresh mushrooms in a little butter over high heat until golden. Set aside.

Soften the onion in olive oil and 30 g of butter over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are translucent at the edges. Add the white wine and stir until absorbed.

Add the warm stock a ladleful at a time, stirring after each addition and waiting until each is mostly absorbed before adding the next. After 15 minutes, stir in the porcini and the fried fresh mushrooms. Continue adding stock for a further 5 to 8 minutes until the rice is just tender with a very slight bite. Remove from the heat.
Beat in the cold butter and the Parmesan vigorously for 1 minute. Season, cover, and rest for 2 minutes. The risotto should flow slowly when the pan is tilted. Serve immediately in warm bowls.
